currentReconciliation.readingRule: The older criterion narratives below remain historical mapping context. This reconciliation supersedes their stale remaining-work statements, not their original criteria or qualification limits. No criterion is accepted by this update.
currentReconciliation.AC01_AC03_AC06_AC07_AC08: Actual missing-Docker and both endpoint negative/corrected-recovery sequences now have independently reviewed native evidence. They supplement existing installed boot, persistence and status checks. Endpoint product output is docker_engine_check_failed, not an errno classifier; recovered aggregate readiness remains degraded and persistence write readiness unknown.
currentReconciliation.AC02_AC04: Keep the existing real broker permission and ordinary-consumer isolation evidence. Docker recovery tests do not prove additional permission, actor or general plugin-host boundaries. P03 service-handle obligations remain later work.
currentReconciliation.AC05: Actual legacy startup/environment/named shutdown evidence is now located in legacy-shell-startup-shutdown-review.json and legacy-native-preservation-review.json. Map those assertions against installed opt-in startup/shutdown and disjoint ownership evidence. Protected-file preservation and final candidate correspondence remain open; do not call both complete paths accepted from this mapping.
currentReconciliation.AC09: Actual owners/noowners tests have run on the retained APFS pair. Same-pair final candidate checks and normal teardown remain required. The five protected-file installed assertion sets remain unqualified because the additional provisioner refused. Remaining installed Compose, image acquisition and runtime cache failures are distinct obligations. Final component/source/retention/pattern/candidate checks remain required.
currentReconciliation.AC10: No phase candidate commit, push, remote verification or advancement decision is established by this reconciliation.
currentReconciliation.FAIL01_FAIL02_FAIL56_FAIL58: Retain each existing narrowly tested scope. Docker endpoint failure does not substitute for NATS endpoint/authentication. Startup-owner death before the first role is not integrated death after partial role creation. Controlled foreign/version refusals are not automatically integrated tests. Do not expand P02 into later federation or injected-handle work.
currentReconciliation.FAIL55_FAIL59: New native negative/recovery cases preserve actual broker, volume and stored record identities. They supplement, rather than replace, final cold/warm/restart/status and failing-service oracles.
currentReconciliation.FAIL57: Missing Docker, permission-denied endpoint and unavailable endpoint have actual corrected recovery evidence. Compose discovery is supplemental only; its installed-host negative and recovery remain pending. Offline image derivation/probe load and a new signed release are preparation, not actual cache refusal or pinned-image acquisition failure. Keep those two image cases distinct.
currentReconciliation.componentCountReview: Main and peer independently enumerated current manifests and task bindings: nine P02-owned components plus REPO-03-C02 and REPO-10-C08 produce eleven distinct components and twenty-three unique behavior checks. The older thirteen-count wording below is unsupported historical bookkeeping, not two missing requirements. Preserve the exact existing check set; no scope reduction or new requirement is implied.

failureScenarios.scenario: Broker absent, wrong endpoint, invalid credentials, or stale deployment configuration
failureScenarios.oracle: Boot reports a specific readiness failure; no hidden fallback channel or hosted-model dependency; retry has bounded noise and does not multiply plugin instances.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Real broker endpoint/auth/TLS/deployment refusal component evidence and installed observation/recovery.
failureScenarios.remaining: Map absent/wrong/auth/stale config separately; no hidden fallback, retry noise/role multiplicity and exact candidate assertions.

failureScenarios.scenario: Ordinary plugin publishes to kernel internals or a kernel reply subject
failureScenarios.oracle: Broker denies it; approved status is readable only at declared scope; service-injection handles do not bypass the boundary. Test exact and wildcard subjects.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: P02 broker exact/wildcard/account/reply/status/SYS/JS denials have real native component evidence.
failureScenarios.remaining: Record per-phase P02 result in gate failureScenarios, preserve global not-run planning matrix and pending P03 service-handle tests. Current Services Clock/Logger absence is not bypass-test evidence.

failureScenarios.scenario: Cold launch with no selected instance, then warm launch from another project directory
failureScenarios.oracle: One owned Compose project reaches actual service and application readiness; the next launch reuses its identity and volumes unchanged. Both display the same scoped status schema.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Actual cold→warm and other-directory reuse, same owned instance/volume/stored record/schema.
failureScenarios.remaining: Bind final candidate and canonical native lifecycle qualification; later client/federation repeats remain later-phase obligations.

failureScenarios.scenario: Two native macOS ARM64 terminals start together; startup owner crashes mid-boot
failureScenarios.oracle: One startup owner and one selected instance; waiting callers receive bounded progress or failure. Stale ownership recovery cannot create duplicate stacks or trust an unrelated PID.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Actual concurrent cold and startup-owner death before first protected role; exact lease release/retry; separate supervisor partial-start rollback.
failureScenarios.remaining: Map mid-boot point honestly and bounded waiters, no PID trust/duplicate stack; current native candidate run and exact preservation ledger.

failureScenarios.scenario: Docker or Compose absent, daemon unavailable, permission denied or image pull fails
failureScenarios.oracle: Bounded actionable diagnostics; no false readiness, privileged installation, secret leakage or retry storm. A later corrected launch can recover without losing data.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Doctor missing-client refusal and generic inspection failures are tested; actual account Compose version mismatch/recovery retained. No reviewed actual named case expressly covers missing Compose/unavailable or denied daemon/pull failure.
failureScenarios.remaining: Identify exact current branch/assertion and safe real negative+corrected-launch/data-retention evidence. Generic inspection_unavailable cannot prove a particular missing subcommand or permission errno. Runtime --pull never differs from preparation image pull; map both contractual cases rather than silently omitting pull failure.

failureScenarios.scenario: Wrong Docker context, another user instance, occupied endpoint or incompatible running release
failureScenarios.oracle: Reject ambiguous or unauthorized attachment; identify selected context and safe next action. Do not start a shadow stack, mutate a remote daemon, silently upgrade or delete volumes.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Actual child-selection conflict and occupied endpoint/recovery; component wrong-owner/version/archive/context refusals.
failureScenarios.remaining: Distinguish controlled response negatives from real-engine integrated evidence; map no-shadow/no-remote-mutation/no-upgrade/no-volume-delete and safe action without adding destructive tests.

failureScenarios.scenario: Partially started or unhealthy stack; readiness timeout; restart after persistent data was written
failureScenarios.oracle: Report the failing service and observed readiness state. Compatible owned recovery retains instance identity and durable data; unsafe recovery stops for a deliberate action. Running containers alone never qualify success.
failureScenarios.currentEvidence: Actual abrupt host restart/stored data, live broker/member loss, partial-start rollback and reconnect exhaustion; healthy-container alone never qualifies readiness.
failureScenarios.remaining: Bind each readiness failure and compatible recovery identity/data oracle to exact final candidate; do not use cached L04-only or synthetic readiness as live role-loss proof.
